audit.why: Emerald+ 52.05% over 876 games, matches the table.

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is never mentioned anywhere in the entry — not in early, mid, late, whys, spikes or wants.
audit.why: This is the single decisive interaction of the lane and it is simply absent. Mundo's passive "resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby". Tahm Kench's entire kill pattern is one immobilise — the 3-stack Tongue Lash stun. Against Mundo the first one does not land at all; he shrugs it and drops a cannister that, if he picks it up, refunds health and cuts the passive's cooldown. Every "threaten the stun at 3 stacks" line in this entry is written as though that passive does not exist.
audit.corrected: The passive is now named in early and whys[1], with the instruction to bait it before committing the real immobilise.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly sells a "Q-stun then Devour" chain as one combo.
audit.why: Riot's own text in the kit: An Acquired Taste — "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion"; Tongue Lash — "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." The stun and the swallow draw on the same three stacks, so a Q cast at 3 stacks stuns and destroys the resource Devour requires. The real sequence is to let Q land the THIRD stack (which does not stun) and then press R.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as: build to three, let Q apply the third stack, Devour immediately; a Q thrown at an enemy already on 3 stacks stuns but burns the swallow.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry credits Tahm Kench with "Abyssal Voyage" 3 time(s) and treats it as a global/roaming ultimate.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage was removed in the Tahm Kench rework. The kit file lists W = Abyssal Dive and R = Devour; there is no global travel ability in the kit at all. Advice built on "use Abyssal Voyage to roam / reposition cross-map" tells the player to press a button that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed to Devour (R) or Abyssal Dive (W) as appropriate, with the surrounding advice rewritten so it describes what those abilities actually do.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: "NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere". Confirmed — the entry names Heart Zapper, Infected Bonesaw and Maximum Dosage but attaches a number to none of them.
audit.why: The three numbers change the plan completely: Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4s, so there is no poke window to wait out — you have to break line of sight behind minions instead. Heart Zapper is 17s at rank 1. Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s, which is the one genuinely long timer in his kit and the only thing worth timing an all-in around.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, phases[3].why and wants.you[1].

audit.why: Anti-heal is already flagged core in breakdown.late and dontsFull[1], which is right: Heart Zapper heals off stored damage and Maximum Dosage heals a percent of missing health. Nothing to add.

edits.before: At levels 1-2 you have the clearest edge in this lane: Tongue Lash's range lets you slow Mundo and stack An Acquired Taste on him without walking into his melee range, and he has no meaningful early heal or escape to punish you for fishing stacks. The moment you hit 3 stacks at level 2, threaten the stun — Mundo cannot disengage and taking a full empowered Devour without any defensive cooldowns online is costly for him. The key threat you must respect even this early is Infected Bonesaw: every cleaver hit removes a chunk of your current HP, which directly shrinks your grey-health bank before Thick Skin can convert it, so do not stand in cleaver range trying to farm if he has lane priority.
edits.after: At levels 1-2 you have the clearest edge in this lane: Tongue Lash's range lets you slow Mundo and stack An Acquired Taste on him without walking into his melee range, and he has no meaningful early heal or escape to punish you for fishing stacks. At 3 stacks pick one: Q stuns and consumes them, Devour needs them intact. Either way Goes Where He Pleases shrugs off your first immobilise and drops a cannister — bait it out before you commit. The key threat you must respect even this early is Infected Bonesaw: every cleaver hit removes a chunk of your current HP, which directly shrinks your grey-health bank before Thick Skin can convert it, so do not stand in cleaver range trying to farm if he has lane priority.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 flip the script. Mundo has enough passive regeneration and Bonesaw cooldown reduction to start winning the war of attrition against your grey-health mechanic — percent-current-HP damage is exactly the damage type Thick Skin cannot sustainably absorb, because it keeps your HP low enough that the grey-health pool stays tiny. He will stand at his Bonesaw range, throw cleavers whenever they are up, and simply walk away if you step toward him, using his movement-speed passive to stay out of Tongue Lash slow range. Play for CS and limit his damage by standing behind minions to block cleaver, and save your Activate E shield for when he commits to a full trade rather than burning it on poke. At 6 both of you gain meaningful power but neither gains a kill window cleanly — your Abyssal Voyage adds global pressure but does nothing for the 1v1; his Maximum Dosage makes a delayed all-in extremely punishing if you misjudge the ult timer.

edits.before: Late game Mundo outscales your ability to remove him: a two-item Mundo sustaining through Maximum Dosage heals more per second than your empowered Devour deals during the hold, and he simply walks back out of the stun window at full HP. Your job shifts entirely to peeling your backline and using Abyssal Voyage to threaten cross-map plays or drop onto a carry he has separated. The 1v1 is a write-off — do not burn Devour trying to hold a champion who heals through it. Your value in teamfights is still enormous: point-and-click stun into Devour on their carry wins the fight even if Mundo himself cannot be killed, and your E shield on an ally can negate his team's dive follow-up.

notes: The packet defect "NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere" is real and now addressed. The larger miss was Goes Where He Pleases: Mundo eats Tahm Kench's first immobilise outright, which invalidates the "threaten the 3-stack stun" framing this entry was built on. I did not touch the claim that Mundo can pick the cannister back up for a cooldown refund beyond what Riot's own text states.
